## 1. Executive summary

**Verdict: the skeleton is buildable, deployable in structure, and the shipped
NASA terrain data is high quality — but the application itself is not
implemented.** Gate S does **not** pass, because one of its hard requirements
(`npm test` green) fails and the 15-feature architecture contract has no
implementation. Everything that can be verified today has been verified.

| Metric | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Checks executed | **55** |
| Passed | **46** |
| Failed | **7** |
| Warnings / informational | **2** |
| Features implemented (of 15) | **0** (1 partial: EN/ES catalogues; 1 data-only: LOLA DEMs) |
| Repository test files (baseline) | **0** (`npm test` exits 1, "No test files found"); after the delta, only the separate `mcp/miro` test exists and the root `npm test` fails to load it (see §0) |
| Build | **PASS** — `vite 8.3.8`, 31 modules, 253 ms |
| `dist/` payload | **11,561,681 B** raw ≈ 11.03 MiB (`du -sh` = 12 MB) |
| JS bundle | **123,346 B** raw / **44,101 B** gzip (+ 929,272 B sourcemap) |
| Terrain data | **10,485,760 B** = 10.00 MiB (≈ 91 % of `dist/`) |
| Data integrity | **PASS** — 2 regions, 0 failures; decoded ranges match declared values exactly; cross-region r = 0.9993 |
| Secrets / local URLs in `dist/` | **none found** |
| Preview server | **PASS** — shell, CSS, JS, all 4 terrain data files 200 with correct MIME and byte-identical content |

At the baseline the three critical blockers, in order, were: (1) `npm test` was red
because there were no tests; (2) the feature modules did not exist, so nothing of the
15-feature contract could be demonstrated; (3) the required `pois.json`, `ephemeris/` and
`layers.json` datasets were missing. **After the delta, blocker (3) is closed** (the
datasets now ship) and (1)/(2) remain — the root test command still fails, now because it
tries to load the separate MCP test file. Details and severity ranking are in section 11.

### B-10 Missing-data behaviour under the SPA fallback — **WARN (deployment risk)**

```bash
curl -sS -D - -o /tmp/b.txt http://127.0.0.1:4173/data/pois.json           # Accept: */*
curl -sS -H 'Accept: application/json' -D - -o /tmp/b.txt http://127.0.0.1:4173/data/pois.json
curl -sS -D - -o /tmp/b.txt http://127.0.0.1:4173/favicon.ico
```

Observed (the missing datasets are expected to be missing today — this check
characterises **how** a missing file behaves):

| Request | Status | Content-Type | Body |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/data/pois.json` (Accept `*/*`) | **200** | `text/html` | the 600 B `index.html` |
| `/data/pois.json` (`Accept: application/json`) | **404** | — | empty |
| `/data/terrain/nope.bin` (Accept `*/*`) | **200** | `text/html` | `index.html` |
| `/data/terrain/nope.bin` (`Accept: application/octet-stream`) | **404** | — | empty |
| `/does-not-exist` | **200** | `text/html` | `index.html` |
| `/favicon.ico` | **404** | — | empty |

Consequence: a loader that checks only `res.ok` will treat a missing data file as
valid and fail later in `JSON.parse` with a confusing HTML error, while a loader
that sends `Accept: application/json` gets a clean 404. **All data checks must
assert `Content-Type` and parse the payload, never trust the status code alone.**
On GoDaddy the same behaviour will occur once the `.htaccess` SPA fallback in
`docs/deployment.md` section 5 is installed. Evidence:
`preview-mime-behavior.txt`, `preview-missing-data-behavior.txt`.

## 4. Data-integrity checks (D)

All D checks were executed with two independent tools:

```bash
node `docs/test-report.md` the repository root/public/data/terrain
python3 `docs/test-report.md`
```

The validator's full output is in `terrain-validation.txt`; its exit code was
**0** ("PASS — 2 regions validated, 0 failures, 0 warning(s)"). Visual previews
are `south-pole-875s-20m-hillshade.png`, `south-pole-80s-80m-hillshade.png`,
`south-pole-*-elevation.png`; raw stats in `terrain-preview-output.txt`.

| ID | Check | Observed result | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D-01 | `index.json` parses, schema fields (`referenceRadiusM`, projection, `defaultRegionId`, 2 regions) | radius 1,737,400 m; `polar_stereographic`; default = `south-pole-875s-20m`; 2 regions | PASS |
| D-02 | Binary size vs `width × height × 2` bytes | high-res 8,388,608 B = 2048×2048×2; wide 2,097,152 B = 1024×1024×2; `meta.grid.fileBytes` matches actual | PASS |
| D-03 | int16 little-endian decode, dtype/endianness/layout declarations | decoded as `<i2` / row-major; all values inside int16 range; no decode errors | PASS |
| D-04 | Decoded min/max vs declared `elevationRangeM` (metadata **and** index) | high-res `[-4378, 2369]` = declared exactly; wide `[-7274, 7001]` = declared exactly | PASS |
| D-05 | Derived pixel size and symmetric bounds | 151,680/2048 = 74.0625 m and 608,000/1024 = 593.75 m, equal to declared; bounds symmetric around the pole (0,0) | PASS |
| D-06 | Coverage vs documented latitude bands (ρ = 2R·tan(π/4+lat/2)) | high-res edge ρ = 75,840 m → **−87.4994°** (expected −87.5°, Δ = 19.6 m = 0.265 px); corner ρ = 107,254 m → −86.4641°; wide edge ρ = 304,000 m → **−80.0002°** (Δ = −5.6 m); corner → −75.8938° | PASS |
| D-07 | Polar-stereographic forward/inverse round-trip at 5 probe points | latitude drift < 1e-9°, longitude drift < 1e-9° | PASS |
| D-08 | Cross-region consistency (high-res vs wide-area, 1,600 paired samples) | Pearson **r = 0.9993**; mean abs difference **28.8 m**; max abs difference **233 m** — consistent given different resampling | PASS |
| D-09 | Visual plausibility (downsampled hillshade + elevation render) | Cratered, coherent lunar south-pole relief in both grids; no noise/constant field; images in `docs/test-report.md` | PASS |
| D-10 | Metadata source geometry | 7584×7584 @20 m = 151,680×151,680 m = grid bounds; 7600×7600 @80 m = 608,000×608,000 m = grid bounds (both consistent) | PASS |
| D-11 | Sentinel/no-data scan (`-32768`, `32767`, zeros) | no int16 sentinels; zeros = 2,256 px (0.054 %) high-res and 191 px (0.018 %) wide, spatially scattered (1,101 distinct rows) → plausible real data, not a stripe | PASS (info) |
| D-12 | Every JSON data file parses | 6/6 files (`public/` + `dist/`) valid JSON | PASS |
| D-13 | Served bytes equal disk bytes | SHA-256 identical for all four data files (see B-09) | PASS |
| D-14 | Terrain decode performance | 8 MiB read 13.7 ms; int16 min/max scan 47.1 ms; 2 MiB read 3.5 ms, scan 50.8 ms (Node, warm cache) | PASS (info) |

Additional observation (recorded for the loader authors): the documented
"87.5S–90S" / "80S–90S" coverage refers to the **edge** radius of the square
grid; the corners extend further north (86.46°S and 75.89°S). The region
selection logic must therefore decide "contains site" using the square bounds
(column/row inside `0..width`, `0..height`), not a circular latitude cutoff.

The current 123 kB JS bundle does not include Three.js or any feature code — once
`src/render` and the services land, expect the initial JS to grow substantially;
the plan's L9 budgets (≤ 250 kB gzip) remain the target. The terrain regions are
the dominant cost: the wide-area region alone is 2 MiB raw (1.69 MiB gzip).

## 11. Blockers and risks (ranked — HISTORICAL baseline findings)

> **Superseded for blockers 1–3, 5–7 and 9:** the missing tests, feature modules, datasets, Three.js/fallback, CI, JSON export and `.htaccess` were resolved after the baseline (`.htaccess` was shipped with the static build in a later deployment-config commit). The historical findings below are kept as the baseline record; current remaining risks are the end-to-end/accuracy/deployment validation described in §0 and §12.


Ranking uses severity for the NASA submission (a disabled demo or a non-deployable
build is critical) × likelihood.

| Rank | Severity | Blocker / risk | Evidence | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **CRITICAL** | `npm test` fails: zero test files, Vitest exits 1 | B-07, U-06 | The documented release pipeline and deployment checklist item "npm test is green" cannot pass; no regression safety for 15 features | Add Vitest unit/contract tests (test bench can supply a starter suite from outside the repo for transfer); make `npm test` a required gate |
| 2 | **CRITICAL** | 0/15 architecture features implemented; app is a placeholder shell | section 10, E-06 | Nothing of the challenge deliverable (site selection, visibility, autopilot, export) can be demonstrated or judged | Implement the contract modules now in the planned priority order (plan section 9); re-run Gate A checks per feature |
| 3 | **HIGH** | Required datasets missing: `pois.json`, `ephemeris/`, `layers.json` | B-10, section 10, `feature-presence.txt` | Features 1–8, 10–13 and 15 have no data source; deployment checklist item "dist/data contains required datasets" fails | Produce pre-computed datasets (`scripts/nasa/`) early; keep provenance/attribution; verify with content-type + JSON schema |
| 4 | **HIGH** | No EN/ES switcher; locale not reflected in `html[lang]`/title; persistence unwired | L-02, L-03, L-04 | Deployment checklist item "Only English in default UI (Spanish via switcher)" fails; challenge language requirement looks incomplete; a11y/SEO issue | Add a visible language switcher wired to `persistLocale`, set `document.documentElement.lang` and a localized title; keep `en` default until the switcher exists |
| 5 | **MEDIUM** | No Three.js scene and no no-WebGL fallback (Three.js installed but unused) | E-06, section 10 | Feature 12 unevaluable; 3D demo is a core challenge expectation | Implement `render/moonScene.js` + `render/fallback2d.js`; test with WebGL disabled |
| 6 | **MEDIUM** | No CI workflow (`.github/` absent) | B-16 | "CI is green for the same commit" cannot be satisfied; regression risk with a team | Add a minimal GitHub Actions workflow (`npm ci`, `npm test`, `npm run build`) via `reviewer-pusher` |
| 7 | **MEDIUM** | No JSON brief export / QuickMap / Moon Trek links | section 10 (F15) | Challenge feature 15 missing; post-deploy check "JSON brief export works" cannot pass | Implement `services/export.js` and its UI action; test schema + download in E2E |
| 8 | **LOW–MEDIUM** | SPA fallback returns **200 `text/html`** for missing data when the client uses default `Accept` | B-10 | Loaders can mise-read missing data as success and crash in `JSON.parse`; future tests can produce false positives | Always validate `Content-Type` in loaders; assert JSON parse + schema in tests; prefer `fetch(url, { headers: { Accept: 'application/json' } })` |
| 9 | **LOW** | No `.htaccess` in `public/`/`dist/` | B-15 | SPA fallback, HTTPS redirect, compression and cache headers are server-side-only; cannot be verified from the build; easy to forget during upload | Add `public/.htaccess` (coordinated change) or keep the manual upload step in the deploy runbook |
| 10 | **LOW** | Missing favicon → console 404 | E-05 | Cosmetic browser console noise; not a blocker | Add a small favicon or a `<link rel="icon">` |
| 11 | **LOW** | Sourcemap 929 kB = 8 % of `dist/` | B-14 | Larger upload/first build size; acceptable per `docs/deployment.md` | Optional: build once with sourcemaps disabled for the demo (Lead decision) |
| 12 | **LOW** | Documentation drift | repo docs | `README.md`/`docs/project.md` still say the stack and challenge are "to be defined"; `docs/deployment.md` lists data files not yet committed; architecture ownership table lists CI that does not exist | Update docs after coding lands; keep architecture as the contract |
| 13 | **INFO** | Payload/performance: 10 MB uncompressed terrain (91 % of dist) | B-05, P-03 | Slow first load on poor venue/4G connections; default region is 8 MiB raw | Enable deflate for `.bin` on the host (68–85 % reduction) or ship the wide-area region for the demo; consider lazy-loading regions |

## 12. Coverage, limitations and honest status

What was actually exercised: the complete build/deploy surface, the real NASA
terrain data (structurally, numerically, visually, and over HTTP), the i18n
catalogue contract and runtime language selection, the placeholder UI in a real
browser at three viewports, plus security and payload hygiene. **46 of 55 checks pass.**

What was **not** testable today, and why:

1. **All functional feature logic** — `src/core`, `src/services`,
   `src/components`, `src/render`, `src/workers` do not exist. Features 1–13 and
   15 have no code path to execute; this report records their absence, not a
   behavioural failure.
2. **Deployed URL checks** (HTTPS, redirect, certificate, GoDaddy headers,
   compression, caching, `.htaccess` behaviour) — the site is not deployed and no
   credentials/hosting were provided; these are marked N/A in
   the deployment checklist run (internal QA evidence).
3. **Post-deploy verification of the EN/ES switcher and JSON export from the
   public URL** — neither feature exists yet.
4. **Re-derivation of the DEMs from the original NASA JP2 files** — source
   granules are not on this machine. Integrity was verified internally
   (dimensions, ranges, coverage, cross-region agreement, checksums, visual
   inspection) against the committed metadata and `scripts/nasa/build-terrain.py`.
5. **Firefox automation** — Firefox 159 is installed but no driver/Playwright is
   set up; only Chromium was automated. A manual Firefox smoke test is advised
   at Gate A.
6. **Component-level unit tests** — no `@vue/test-utils`/`jsdom` installed; the
   throwaway Vitest harness covers pure catalogues only.
7. **Live Horizons dependency** — the dev proxy was only smoke-tested for
   reachability; production must not depend on it (per architecture), and no
   production path calls it.

Repo hygiene statement: the checks regenerated `node_modules/` (`npm ci`) and
`dist/` (`npm run build`) — both are gitignored build artefacts. `git status`
was empty after the run, and the tracked-file index (staged hashes) was
byte-identical to the baseline recorded before the run
(`baseline-tracked-index.txt` vs final diff). One test-bench evidence file was
accidentally written into the repo root during a `curl` probe and was moved out
to `docs/test-report.md` immediately; the repository was
clean afterwards.
